narrative.northStar: A Native Mac App in the Browser
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "A Native Mac App in the Browser"**

HelpDesky should feel like it shipped alongside macOS Mail, Reminders and System Settings. The window is a calm grey ground. A translucent source-list sidebar sits on the left. Work happens in white inset groups with hairline shadows, and every action is system blue. The commitment is to convention, carried out with care: nothing invents a bespoke look, so colleagues already know how everything works the first time they see it.

The same tokens serve three registers. Sign-in and registration are a single centred panel in the style of an Apple ID screen. The staff side is a source-list app: large titles, segmented controls, a rounded search field, and a white table group that reads like a Mail message list. The end-user portal swaps the sidebar for a translucent top bar over one centred column, and tells each person where their ticket stands in plain words inside a coloured capsule. Status and priority use Apple's system colours. Shape and placement say what a mark is (a capsule for priority, a dot and a label for status), and colour confirms it.
keyCharacteristics: System font only (San Francisco on Apple devices, Segoe UI Variable on Windows). Hierarchy comes from weight, size and tight negative tracking.
Window Grey ground, white groups on 12px corners with a hairline-plus-whisper shadow, and Separator lines inside them.
One action colour (System Blue) for buttons, links, the selected sidebar row and focus.
Segmented controls on a Control Fill track with a white raised segment, never tabs or underlines.
Capsule priority tags, dot-plus-label statuses, avatar-plus-name assignees and a dashed "Unassigned" capsule.
Glass is only for chrome: the staff sidebar and the portal top bar blur what scrolls beneath them (saturate 180%, blur 20px).

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: System Blue is the only interactive colour. Status, priority and availability hues describe state; they are never buttons or links.

rules.name: The Shape-Carries-Meaning Rule
rules.body: Priority is always a tinted capsule (wash background, ink text, 7px leading dot). Staff status is always a 7px ink dot followed by an Ink label, with no fill. Assignment is an avatar and first name, or a dashed "Unassigned" capsule. On the staff side, a status never becomes a filled capsule and a priority never becomes a bare dot. On the portal, the status phrase is the one exception: it is a capsule in the status wash, because there it is the headline.

rules.name: The Same-Hue-Everywhere Rule
rules.body: A status or priority uses the same ink in a dot, a capsule, a portal phrase, a timeline dot and a Reports chart bar. Charts that do not show status (category, volume over time) use Graphite, never System Blue.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels or tracked-out captions. Headers, captions, badges and buttons are sentence case at 0 tracking, the way macOS sets them.

rules.name: The Say-It-In-Words Rule
rules.body: End users never see a raw status enum. Their status phrases come from one vocabulary (`client/src/utils/ticketStatus.js`): "Waiting for IT", "With {first name}", "{first name} is working on it" or "Being worked on", and "Fixed". Staff see the short labels Open, In progress and Resolved.

rules.name: The Glass-Is-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur (saturate 180%, blur 20px) belongs only to persistent chrome: the staff sidebar and the portal top bar. Content groups are opaque white.

dos: **Do** wrap every new screen in `.app-shell`, `.auth-screen` or `.portal-shell` so it picks up the scoped macOS tokens. Outside those wrappers, the legacy `:root` values apply.
**Do** use System Blue (#0071e3) for actions, links, the selected row and focus, and nothing else.
**Do** put content in white 12px groups with the hairline shadow on Window Grey (#f5f5f7), with Separator (#e5e5ea) lines inside.
**Do** use a segmented control on a Control Fill (#e8e8ed) track for any switch between two to five views.
**Do** collect related inputs in a grouped-field box with sentence-case captions inside each cell.
**Do** show priority as a tinted capsule, staff status as a dot and label, and assignment as an avatar and name or the dashed Unassigned capsule.
**Do** keep segmented controls on one row on mobile, within the page margins, scrolling sideways if they overflow.
**Do** pair every animation with a `prefers-reduced-motion` override.
**Do** use the supplied logo image for the brand mark wherever HelpDesky identifies itself.
donts: **Don't** set labels, headers or captions in uppercase or with letter-spacing.
**Don't** fill a staff status as a capsule, or use status and priority hues for buttons or links.
**Don't** add borders to cards. The hairline shadow is the edge.
**Don't** use backdrop blur on content groups. Glass is for the sidebar and the portal bar.
**Don't** fade a disabled primary button to pale blue. Use Control Fill with Secondary Label text.
**Don't** show end users raw status enums.
**Don't** add a bespoke brand typeface or accent colour. The system font and the system palette are the identity.
knownGaps: Admin **Ticket Settings** (`TicketMetaAdmin.jsx`) and **Reports** (`Reports.jsx`) inherit the tokens through the generic card, form-group, button and table rules, with no bespoke macOS treatment. Reports still uses `--bar-track`, which exists only in legacy `:root` (#ebecf0), and its PDF export hard-codes the old navy and grey print styles.
**Avatars** are pastel circles that still use the six legacy wash/ink pairs hard-coded in `Avatar.jsx` (for example #deebff / #0747a6), not the macOS status palette.

**Legacy `:root` tokens** (#0052cc primary, #172b4d text, #f4f5f7 ground and the old status inks) remain under the scoped overrides, and so do base rules with 3px and 6px corners and uppercase captions that the macOS section overrides. They are not the system.

**Portal tone rules** (`--tone-rule` #b3d4ff, #c0b6f2, #abf5d1) and the confirmation band's #b3d4ff border are legacy hues that the macOS section has not retuned. They still draw the status band's divider.
**Orphaned app-icon CSS:** the `.app-icon` and `.app-icon-large` gradient-tile rules in the macOS section no longer have any markup that uses them, because the logo image replaced them.
**Tertiary Label** (#86868b) on the sidebar glass is roughly 3.2:1, which is below 4.5:1 for the 11px section captions.
**Resolved Green** (#1f7a36) on its wash is about 3.9:1. That is below 4.5:1 for the 12px Low priority capsule and the 18px/600 portal "Fixed" capsule.
